originality.rationale: Compared the exact graph, uncentered ball family, real strong ell2 norm, cubic spectral formulation, and eighteen-extremizer classification against published-finding corpus semantic searches, closely related exact analytic invariants, and primary full-text research. The closest centered triangular-prism result considers only balls centered at their output vertices; it is strictly smaller and cannot imply the uncentered theorem. Soria–Tradacete (2014) has its general best-constant theorem in 0<p<=1 and centered operators; González-Riquelme–Madrid (2020) defines uncentered operators but the known strong ell2 results are for centered stars and complete graphs; González-Riquelme–Kovač–Madrid (2026) treats variation and graphs of at most five vertices. No inspected result provides a dominating, dual, equivalent or tabulated value for this six-vertex uncentered strong ell2 claim. Absolute priority remains unproven and indexed search is not exhaustive.

value.rationale: The triangular prism is the canonical vertex-transitive six-vertex cubic Cartesian product C3 square K2, so the quantity is a natural analytic invariant rather than an arbitrary coordinate slice. The theorem discovers a strict increase upon freeing averaging centers even on a vertex-transitive graph, and its sharp constant is a cubic algebraic number with a complete two-orbit (6 and 12) extremizer classification. Such graph-symmetry inequivalent equality classes tied at the exact optimum provide a useful structural test for any theory of graph-product maximal averages. The result is self-contained, exact and motivated by the finite-graph maximal-norm problem; no unsupported generalization to larger prisms is claimed.
